en: Now follows the surrender to Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa.
[I bow to] Śrī, the supreme beloved of Viṣṇu, the Lord of this world and Master of Veṅkaṭa, who delights in her eternal residence upon His chest, who increases His forbearance,
whose sprout-like hands are adorned with lotuses, and who sits upon a lotus throne.
I bow to the Blessed Mother of the World, radiant with the virtues of maternal affection and the like.
O glorious one, ocean of compassion, creator of all worlds, omniscient, omnipotent, lover of those who prostrate before you, sovereign of all!

O Lord, O Pārijāta tree easily accessible through virtuous conduct, I take refuge at the feet of Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, upon which well-formed, fragrant flowers have been offered along with anklets. 2. Upon which well-formed, fragrant flowers... [are placed].

I take refuge in the feet of Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, which possess fragrance and create fragrance, which are perfectly symmetrical, which are gentle, and which, though ever experienced, remain ever-new to be experienced. 3.

They were completely erasing the report of the likeness between [their faces] and a lotus— [a lotus] which possesses a thick redness that blooms instantly upon rising and is filled with fragrance— even while they were engaged in acts of bold daring.
I take refuge in the feet of Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa,
which are marked with lines forming the banner, the nectar-pitcher, the parasol, the thunderbolt, the goad, the lotus, the wish-fulfilling tree, the conch, and the discus.
I take refuge in the feet of the glorious Veṅkaṭeśa, whose soles are adorned with auspicious marks that signify the supreme reality;
I take refuge in the feet of the illustrious Veṅkaṭeśa, which surpass the sapphire with their external splendors, and which, by the rising rays of their nails, cast off the luster of the moon. 6.

Their hands, like tender sprouts from a bed of lotuses, instantly grew weary even while massaging [her] with love and fear; for their softness was beyond the reach of the eyes, speech, and mind of their beloved.
I take refuge at the feet of Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa—
[the feet] whose natural splendor corresponds to that of Lakṣmī and Mahī, and which are touched by the sprout-like hands of his divine consorts, Nīlā and the others.

I take refuge in the feet of the illustrious Veṅkaṭeśa, which, it is said, have become deeply red through the transition [of the sun] at dawn; [feet] that are the crest-jewels of the infinite multitudes of Brahmās, Viṣṇus, Śivas, and others. 8.

[And] the eternal... [of food]... [and] the rites of Śiva and others. 9. [And] the crown of... [the gods]. 10. [And] the multitude of... [the sages]. 11. [And] the multitude of... [the ancestors]. 12. [And] the multitude of... [the stars]. 13. [And] the multitude of... [the mountains]. 14. [And] the multitude of... [the oceans]. 15. [And] the multitude of... [the rivers]. 16. [And] the multitude of... [the universes]. 21. [And] the multitude of... [the beings]. 22. [And] the multitude of... [the dharmas]. 23. [And] the multitude of... [the truths]. 24. [the avatars]. 61. [And] the multitude of... [the incarnations]. 62. [And] the multitude of... [the forms]. 63. [And] the multitude of... [the bodies]. 64. [And] the multitude of... [the faces]. 65. [And] the multitude of... [the eyes]. 66. [And] the multitude of... [the hands]. 67. [And] the multitude of... [the feet]. 68. [And] the multitude of... [the attributes].
I take refuge in the feet of Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, which perform the noble rite of lustration with the sprouting splendors of newly set, blazing precious gems. 9.

The two verses beginning with "In the highest step of Viṣṇu" (viṣṇoḥ pade parame) are praises of its transcendence, while those beginning with "the spring of honey" (madhva utsaḥ) are grasped as objects of enjoyment; furthermore,
the latter are likewise presented in the palm of Your hand.
I take refuge at the feet of Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa. O Pārtha, those very feet of his which were shown by you alone as a worthy charioteer—unto them I go for refuge. ||10||
Once again, I take refuge in the glorious feet of Veṅkaṭeśa, which were shown to me here by the hand [of the Lord];
upon my head [rest] the hoods of Kāliya, and in the vast forests— ||11||
Upon the peak of Śrī Veṅkaṭādri, the crest of the Vedas.
With minds focused on nothing else, I take refuge in the feet of Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, which are equally honored by those who have attained meditative absorption,
and upon whose stainless, joyous surface flowers are strewn. 12.12a-12.12b (part)
I take refuge in these two feet of Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, which serve as the ornament for the peak of the glorious Veṅkaṭādri mountain, and which bring delight to all minds and eyes. 13.
Generally, for the people who have sought refuge, those two [teachings]—
which are like the mother’s breasts providing nectar to a child— are both difficult to fathom at first; yet, though they differ in their incomparable limits, they have attained a mutual equality.
I take refuge at the feet of Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa—
whose lotus feet are constantly served by those preeminent in goodness, and whose sidelong glances are moist with compassion that delivers one from the cycle of worldly existence.
Those two feet of Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, shown to me by the gentle sage who was my husband, I take refuge in.
O Lord of Śrī, through the goddess Śrī acting as Ghaṭikā, you have become the means for my attainment. ||15||

O Lord of the Bull Hill, may I never again be anything other than Your servant— unto You who are eternally resorted to, who possess faultless qualities, and who, being attainable by Your own grace, manifest Yourself as the one to be approached. 16.
Thus ends the *Śrīveṅkaṭeśaprapatti*.
